thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: multiple OOMs observed on inference-worker pods in us-west-2 pool (rwd-gpu-21..rwd-gpu-24). Severity P1. Auto-evict scaling engaged.
jen-oncall: taking pager. tagging eng-runtime and infra. brief status here while I triage.
marco: I'm seeing heavy tail latencies and internal retries on /v1/chat for chat-xlarge. Error budget spike ~3.8% across the pool.
dee: I pulled node metrics — GPU memory usage near 39GB/40GB on two nodes and free fragmentation pattern shows many ~64KiB free blocks; allocator failing to satisfy 256KiB contiguous allocations. nvidia-smi snapshot below.
```
Sat Mar 15 11:05:12 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.89.02    Driver Version: 525.89.02    CUDA Version: 12.1 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB
| Memory-Usage: 39620MiB / 40960MiB
| GPU-Util: 92%
| Fragmentation-score: HIGH (many small free chunks, median free-chunk 64KiB)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Processes: inference-worker (pid 5421) ~ 38400MiB resident
```
yuan: runtime logs show repeated failed allocations: "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (required 262144)" around 11:04:50Z, followed by soft-retry loop and request resubmission. attaching snippet.
infra-bot: Created incident ticket INC-20260315-042 on Jira and linked metrics dashboards.
jen-oncall: immediate mitigation ideas? we need low-risk actions we can take without rolling the runtime.
marco: quick options:
- reduce route max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 for chat-xlarge (should reduce per-request working set)
- flip a runtime flag to enable "kv-prefetch-limits=512" so we don't prefetch indefinitely for long contexts
- cordon one node and shift traffic away while we collect heap/alloc traces
these are config-only, no code deploy needed.
dee: agree. also recommend a single controlled restart of inference-worker on the worst node to defragment GPU memory (evicts all allocations). small risk of in-flight requests but acceptable for a P1 mitigation.
yuan: if we restart, we should first shift 30% of traffic to chat-large-quant to avoid customer impact. support to coordinate with customers.
support: on call with impacted customer A and B; they accept a brief brief degraded period and prefer retries rather than failures. they approved 30% traffic shift.
jen-oncall: plan: 1) change max_batch_tokens to 1024 for chat-xlarge in us-west-2 2) set kv-prefetch-limits=512 3) reroute 30% traffic to chat-large-quant 4) restart inference-worker on rwd-gpu-22 if memory not recovered. executing now, stepwise. I'll post timestamps.
jen-oncall: 11:10Z - updated route config (max_batch_tokens=1024) across us-west-2.
jen-oncall: 11:11Z - kv-prefetch-limits=512 enabled via runtime feature flag.
jen-oncall: 11:12Z - traffic-skew applied: 30% to chat-large-quant for affected customers.
marco: dashboards show immediate drop in 95th latency and error-rate starting at 11:13Z. good signal.
dee: memory resident on rwd-gpu-22 dropped from 38400MiB -> 21000MiB by 11:14Z. fragmentation metrics improving.
jen-oncall: 11:16Z - performing controlled restart of inference-worker on rwd-gpu-22. cordoned, drained, restart in progress.
infra-bot: Restart completed on rwd-gpu-22 at 11:17:08Z.
yuan: after restart, allocator maps show contiguous large free segments ~3.5GiB. no further cudaMalloc OOMs reported in logs.
support: customer error-rate back to baseline, they confirm degraded requests recovered. closing their active support tickets. :tada:
marco: hypotheses for RCA (capture here):
- H1: KV-prefetch + large max_batch_tokens created many pinned GPU prefix buffers leading to fragmentation (primary).
- H2: Recent change to runtime allocator bucketization increased frequency of medium-size allocations -> worse fragmentation under mixed-size patterns (secondary).
- H3: simultaneous autoscale + partial eviction sequence left many transient freed blocks that weren't coalesced (contributor).
